Credit Freeze Grips Jordan’s Gas & Water Utilities Sector, Firms Slash Operations and Jobs

AMMAN, June 16—A deepening credit freeze has struck Jordan’s Gas & Water Utilities industry, forcing firms across the sector to slash operations, delay infrastructure projects, and lay off hundreds of workers, industry sources said on Sunday.

The crisis erupted last week after several major lenders withheld new credit lines from utility providers, citing concerns over rising sectoral debt and unstable revenue streams. According to the Jordan Utilities Association, outstanding short-term debt across the industry has soared by 22% since the start of the year, while cash reserves have fallen sharply.

“We’re facing unprecedented liquidity constraints,” said Sami Barakat, spokesperson for the association. “Many companies are now unable to finance routine maintenance or ongoing pipeline upgrades. Some have had to suspend water treatment projects indefinitely.”

At least three regional gas and water supply companies, including Eastern Waters Co. and Petra Gas Holdings, have announced staff reductions affecting a combined 470 employees. Union representatives warned that further job cuts are likely as smaller firms struggle to meet payroll obligations.

Industry analyst Hala Nuseibeh described the situation as “a perfect storm of tightening credit, high debt, and falling demand, particularly in northern governorates.” She noted that several utilities have introduced partial service reductions to conserve resources.

Projects to expand water distribution networks in Irbid and Zarqa have been put on hold, and scheduled upgrades to aging gas pipelines in the capital have been postponed pending new financing.

Barakat called for “urgent intervention” from policymakers to restore confidence and liquidity to the sector. “If this freeze continues, the ability of our industry to provide reliable service is at risk,” he said.

The government has yet to announce any relief measures. The situation remains fluid.
